display: Muralist in São Paulo (Vila Madalena): big birds in flat colour on walls, prints and stickers at the Benedito Calixto weekend fair, and drums in a band.

signals.text: A wall piece of mine ended up on a streetwear brand's T-shirt without anyone asking me, and I'm trying to work out what a fair response looks like.
I want to defend my work without burning a door I might need later, and without being the person who lets it go.
I'm looking for someone who knows Brazilian copyright and trademark law as it applies to murals in public places.
I have a half-finished 8 x 5 m heron mural on Rua Wisard and the rain keeps interrupting it. I need dry days and a way to protect the wall.
The Garças print series (six bird prints, editions of 50) is signed and numbered. I'm looking for more places to sell it beyond my weekend fair.
I'm launching new prints at the fair on 18 October and would like more people to show up.
My income is irregular and low, so a commission, a collaboration or a bulk print order would make a real difference this month.
A family member is frail after a fall and lives alone far away, and I'm trying to help from São Paulo.
My arms feel spent after painting all day, but drumming on Thursdays resets me. I'd like more time to play.
The spray smell from my studio bothers a neighbour of forty years, and I'd like a better ventilation or low-odour setup.
I'm angry about how my work was used, and part of me is embarrassed that my first reaction was pride.
I'd like to hear how other street artists have handled brands using their work uncredited.

offers.text: Mural painting: forty-plus walls across São Paulo since 2019, from three-storey buildings to garage doors, in a style of big birds in flat colour with grain.
Access to scaffolding and a ladder-truck rental contact, so I can scope and reach tall walls.
Montana and Molotow spray cans and the practical know-how for outdoor large-format work.
Limited-edition art prints on Hahnemühle paper (editions of 50) through a local print shop, plus stickers.
A weekend stall at the Praça Benedito Calixto fair with steady foot traffic, which could host another artist's work or a launch.
An Instagram audience of about 14k, mostly local and Latin American, for sharing collaborations or projects I believe in.
Drumming for bands or recordings; I play in a band that rehearses on Thursdays in Pinheiros.
Documentation of my own wall pieces (original photos, dates) that can serve as a model for artists who need to prove authorship.
Experience in the Vila Madalena street-art scene: which walls, owners and permissions work, and who to ask.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I run a café in Vila Madalena with a blank side wall. Do you take commissions for a bird mural, and what would it cost?
catchers.can: I can scope the wall, give a price and a timeline, and arrange scaffolding or a ladder truck. The design is mine, not a fixed corporate message.
catchers.confirm: Is the wall yours or does the owner agree, and are you open to the artist choosing the composition rather than dictating a message?

catchers.hypo: I'm a lawyer who works with creators' rights. A brand printed a mural on a T-shirt and I'd like to help the artist send a proper notice.
catchers.can: I have the screenshots, dates and original photos organised, and a draft notice reviewed by a law-student friend. I'd welcome an experienced second opinion.
catchers.confirm: Do you have specific experience with copyright or trademark claims over murals or public art in Brazil, not just general IP?

catchers.hypo: My brand wants to license a street artist's work properly, with credit and payment. Can you introduce me to artists who would be open to that?
catchers.can: I can talk with you about a licence for one of my pieces, or point you to other artists in the scene who work this way.
catchers.confirm: Are you proposing a licence with credit and payment agreed up front, rather than asking for the artwork first?

catchers.hypo: My grandmother lives alone in a small town in Minas Gerais and she's frail. Do you know anyone who could check in on elderly people there?
catchers.can: I can tell you what has helped in my own family. Through my mum, who is closer to the situation, I may be able to point you to a practical resource in Minas.
catchers.confirm: Is the person you're asking about an older relative living alone in a small town, rather than someone needing professional medical care?

catchers.hypo: I'm a photographer and I document street art. Would you let me shoot your Rua Wisard heron as it progresses?
catchers.can: I can give you access to the wall and its stages, and credit you. A close photographer friend of mine may also have documentation tips.
catchers.confirm: Would you credit me as the muralist wherever the photos appear, and are the photos for documentation or editorial use rather than product merchandise?

catchers.hypo: We run a small gallery or concept store and would like to stock numbered art prints from local artists.
catchers.can: I have the Garças series (six birds, editions of 50, signed and numbered) at R$180 unframed and R$280 framed, with artist proofs kept back.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking to stock finished, numbered prints on consignment or wholesale, and not to reproduce my images on other products?

catchers.hypo: Our band needs a drummer for a few shows. You rehearse regularly, would you consider sitting in?
catchers.can: I can sit in or guest-drum, and I could also introduce you to my band, who are always up for a shared bill.
catchers.confirm: Do the shows avoid Saturday afternoons, when I'm at the fair?

catchers.hypo: I'm an artist whose work was used on products without credit. How did you decide what to do?
catchers.can: I can share what I've done so far (documenting everything, getting a legal read, drafting notices) and what I'm still weighing.
catchers.confirm: Is the issue unauthorised commercial use of a specific work you made, rather than a style you feel was imitated?

catchers.hypo: I'm a neighbour of a studio and the paint smell is a problem. How can artists and neighbours get along?
catchers.can: I know the situation from the inside: an elderly neighbour complained, and a conversation and a small gesture helped. I can describe what worked and look at low-odour options.
catchers.confirm: Is this an ongoing studio-neighbour dispute that can still be settled by talking, rather than one already at the stage of a formal complaint?

forbids.text: I don't paint over other artists' walls.
I don't take corporate commissions that require a fixed message.
I don't do weekend work on Saturday fair days.
I won't pursue legal action that would cost more than a month of my income.
I won't share my home address or my family's names.

projects.name: Garças print edition launch
projects.text: Six bird prints in editions of 50, launching at the weekend fair on 18 October. I'm looking for places and people to help sell and show them.

projects.name: Credit and licensing for street-art on merchandise
projects.text: A response to an uncredited mural-on-T-shirt case, possibly turning it into a model for how brands and muralists can license work with credit and pay.

policy.t1: When there is a real hint of a fit, I'll share the story of the T-shirt, the documentation I've collected, and how I'm weighing my options.
policy.t2: Once the match looks strong and the other person is clear, I'll talk about my money situation and my family's health.
policy.never: My home address and my family members' names.
